text:
incidents-bot: Pager alert triggered: elevated 5xx and p95 latency observed for Hosted API and Dedicated pools in eu-west-3. Error spike correlates with increased STS/KMS egress latency to AWS. Auto-escalation to on-call SRE.

pagerduty-bot: Paging on-call: alex.sre (primary) — please acknowledge.

alex.sre: ack — I'm on it. seeing a sharp jump in 5xx across gateway and runtime for requests routed to eu-west-3. Graphs: http://obs.internal/graphs/incident/1767890123

observability-bot: Summary metrics (last 5m): total requests +27%, 5xx rate +12% -> 18% for eu-west-3, p95 latency 2.3s -> 6.9s. Traces show long STS/KMS calls and socket timeouts to 3rd-party auth egress endpoints.

priya.infra: confirmed from infra side — our NATGW EGRESS metrics to AWS STS endpoints show elevated latency and increased TLS handshake retries. Could be inter-AZ network degradation or upstream provider flapping. AWS status shows "europe-west" anomalies in observed third-party egress in some zones.

alex.sre: action plan: 1) failover routing: divert new hosted-api traffic away from eu-west-3 to eu-west-1/2 where possible (weight 0.2->0.0). 2) flip Dedicated pool routing fallback to regional compatible variants. 3) enable stricter retries/backoff and short-circuit auth calls where token cached. 4) notify support & product for customer comms.

sam.product: noted. I'll prep a short external note draft for status page: brief impact, affected regions, mitigation in progress, ETA unknown. Support team standby for customer messages.

marco.support: prepping templates. Which customers are on Dedicated pools in eu-west-3? sending list to #sales-private.

alex.sre: Marco — run the query: 
```
select customer_id from dedicated_allocations where region='eu-west-3' and active=true;
```
I got ~18 accounts with reserved pools; none in paged-critical tier but several on SLO-sensitive workloads.

priya.infra: rolling targeted route changes now. Pushing a temporary routing policy to edge-router to bias away from eu-west-3: 
```
curl -X POST https://edge-control/api/routes -d '{"region_preference":{"eu-west-3":0.1,"eu-west-1":0.45,"eu-west-2":0.45}}'
```
Applying...

observability-bot: Routing change observed at 1767890350. New traffic distribution taking effect. Error rate for eu-west-3 slowly reducing but still above baseline.

alex.sre: Short-term mitigations applied: route bias, increase auth token TTL for cached tokens to avoid STS calls where safe (non-privileged flows), and rate-limit noisy clients in eu-west-3. Priya, can we enable a circuit-breaker to stop auth backend calls after 50% error to avoid cascading?

priya.infra: enabling circuit-breaker on auth proxy now (threshold 50% 1m). Patch applied and rolling to edge proxies.

pagerduty-bot: Handoff to second-level oncall: priya.infra (escalation) at 1767890500.

priya.infra: digging into NATGW metrics — connection resets and increased SYN retransmits from a subset of eu-west-3 AZs. AWS support ticket opened: https://console.aws/support/cases/CASE-249832. They've acknowledged and investigating third-party egress performance to STS/KMS.

alex.sre: Customer impact assessment: Hosted API: degraded latency and ~10-15% elevated 5xx for routes pinned to eu-west-3 for the last 18m. Dedicated pools: some customer requests hitting reserved nodes in affected AZs experiencing 5xx/timeouts. No mass data loss.

sam.product: Priority customers flagged. Will coordinate with CSMs. Prepare an internal postmortem template.

marco.support: Sent initial customer advisory to impacted accounts: short note, mitigation steps, expected next update in 30m.

observability-bot: Additional detail: sample error trace: 
```
error: upstream_auth_timeout at runtime/runtime.go:312
request_id=abc123 auth_call=sts:GetCallerIdentity latency=5.8s tcp_rtt=1.2s tls_handshake=2.5s
```

alex.sre: Temporary hotfix suggestion (if needed for high priority customers): move their Dedicated pools to eu-west-1 manually (requires plan and short restart). Priya, estimate time for a manual migration?

priya.infra: Live migration runbook: 1) allocate compatible host in eu-west-1 (5-10m), 2) sync KV cache snapshot (if needed) 3) restart worker with pinned model version (3-5m). Total ~20-30m per pool with minimal downtime if we perform staggered restarts.

marco.support: Any requests from customers for manual migration yet? Not yet. I'll wait for formal approval.

alex.sre: ok — hold for now unless a customer escalates. Continue monitoring. Priya, keep AWS support case open and get ETA.

priya.infra: AWS replied: "we are investigating elevated egress latencies in a subset of eu-west-3 AZs, no ETA yet. We'll update within 30m." Case updated: CASE-249832.

observability-bot: 1767890800 metrics: eu-west-3 5xx down from 18%->9% but p95 still elevated ~4.2s. Traffic reroute helped.

alex.sre: good improvement. Let's keep the circuit-breaker and route bias for another 2 hours then reassess. Open action items:
- Alex: keep incident thread and update every 15m
- Priya: own AWS case and circuit-breaker (in progress)
- Marco: customer comms and list of impacted Dedicated pools
- Sam: status page draft + exec brief

sam.product: Posted status update draft to #status-drafts. Please review: 
"We are experiencing elevated latency and errors for API requests routed to eu-west-3 due to a third-party egress issue affecting authentication calls. We have re-routed traffic and applied safeguards; mitigation in progress. Next update in 30 minutes."

marco.support: Approved. Posting to status page now.

observability-bot: 1767891400: error rate stable ~6%, p95 trending down to 3.1s.

alex.sre: minor follow-up: ensure we collect a sample of failing request IDs for postmortem and attach to ticket. Use: 
```
select request_id, timestamp, route, status_code from request_logs where region='eu-west-3' and status_code>=500 and timestamp>='2026-03-10T10:00:00Z' limit 200;
```

priya.infra: AWS updated case: "we have isolated a noisy upstream peering causing intermittent packet loss for some AZs; mitigation in progress, traffic shifting recommended."

marco.support: support team sent second customer update referencing status page and mitigation steps. No urgent escalations so far.

alex.sre: bringing this down to monitor-only in 30m unless we see regressions. Leaving routing bias & circuit-breaker in place. If AWS declares region healthy, we'll gradually revert.

pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged resolved -> monitoring mode at 1767891723.

alex.sre: thanks all — excellent coordination. We'll open a postmortem and include timeline, mitigation decisions, and recommendations: add automated fallback for auth egress, widen multi-region routing earlier, and a playbook for Dedicated pool migrations.

sam.product: noted — will schedule post-incident review with SRE, Infra, Support, and Sales.

marco.support: closing support advisory loop — customers notified and tickets updated.

incidents-bot: Thread closed (monitoring).
